summary.headline: Good, debt-light power producer, but contracts behind 60% of revenue expire within months: at Rs 15 the price assumes they renew at today's tariff
summary.text: Vallibel Power Erathna (VPEL.N0000) runs three mini-hydro plants (21.75 MW) and, since September 2025, a 10 MW solar farm, all selling to the state grid. It passes all four business tests: ROE has been 20-45%, net debt is only Rs 0.32bn, it has not made a loss in ten years and profit turns into cash. The problem is timing. The 15-year contracts of its two subsidiary plants, Kiriwaneliya (December 2026) and Denawaka (February 2027), earned Rs 921mn, 60% of 2025/26 revenue, at about Rs 25 a kWh, and their renewal tariff is not disclosed. The group's own renewed plant, Erathna, earns Rs 8.26 a kWh. Recent profit also looks better than it is: 2025/26 included a Rs 421mn one-off tax credit and 2024/25 Rs 479mn of late-payment interest from the CEB. On a first full year after renewal, with the tariff at Erathna's level (bear), halfway (base) or unchanged (bull), EPS is Rs 0.45 / 0.83 / 1.13. At a 14.2% cost of equity (beta 0.58) the five methods give a fair value of about Rs 5.73; buy below Rs 4.87, strong buy below Rs 4.29. At Rs 15.00 the share is well above even the bull case (Rs 9.64). Category: watch list (good business, price too high).

highlights.title: Six months to 30 September 2026 (unaudited)
highlights.text: Revenue rose 43% to Rs 1,107mn, with Rs 231mn from the new solar farm and better rain at the subsidiary plants; owners' profit rose 17% to Rs 497mn (EPS Rs 0.66 against Rs 0.57). Finance cost on the solar loans was Rs 75mn (Rs 2mn a year earlier).

highlights.title: September quarter
highlights.text: Revenue +62% to Rs 571mn, but tax jumped to Rs 168mn (Rs 58mn) after the subsidiary paid the company a Rs 430mn net dividend in July, so owners' profit rose only 21% to Rs 225mn (EPS Rs 0.30 against Rs 0.25).

highlights.title: 2025/26: one-offs on both sides
highlights.text: Revenue +12% to Rs 1,538mn and profit +21% to Rs 1,345mn, but profit before tax fell 32% to Rs 1,046mn: 2024/25 had Rs 479mn of CEB late-payment interest, and 2025/26 had a Rs 421mn deferred tax credit from the solar plant's 100% capital allowance. Capex Rs 1.58bn, mostly borrowed (Rs 1.30bn of term loans).

highlights.title: Two contracts end within four months
highlights.text: Kiriwaneliya's power purchase agreement expires in December 2026 and Denawaka's in February 2027. Renewal is subject to agreement with the CEB and the tariff is not disclosed; they earn about Rs 25 a kWh today against Rs 8.26 at Erathna, renewed in 2019.

models.name: Whole-company DCF (WACC, less net debt) + deferred tax and old-tariff months
models.comment: The plants are valued as a whole company on the first full year after both renewals. Cash after maintenance capex is Rs 0.38 / 0.71 / 0.93bn: owners' share of after-tax operating profit of Rs 0.38 / 0.67 / 0.89bn, plus depreciation of Rs 0.17bn, less maintenance capex of Rs 0.17 / 0.13 / 0.13bn. Growth 0 / 1.5 / 2% for five years, then 1.5 / 2 / 2.5%, paid for at a 10 / 13 / 15% return on new capital, discounted at WACC 15.6 / 14.1 / 12.7%, less net debt of Rs 0.32bn. Value after year 5 is 47-61% of the total. Add Rs 0.23 a share for the deferred tax asset and Rs 0.08 / 0.04 / 0 for the months left at the old tariff.

models.name: P/E method
models.comment: EPS of the first full year after renewal of Rs 0.45 / 0.83 / 1.125 times 5.9 / 7.2 / 8.7, the forward P/E justified at the cost of equity when growth is paid for: payout = 1 - growth / ROE, with ROE 9 / 16 / 22% and growth 1.5 / 2 / 2.5%. Base EPS is 54% below the Rs 1.79 run-rate for two specific reasons: the run-rate includes a one-off Rs 421mn tax credit (about Rs 0.56 a share), and the subsidiary contracts that earn 60% of revenue expire in December 2026 and February 2027.

models.name: Justified price to book
models.comment: (ROE - growth) / (cost of equity - growth) x NAV of Rs 5.01, with ROE 9 / 16 / 22%, growth 1.5 / 2 / 2.5% and cost of equity 15.7 / 14.2 / 12.7%: 0.53 / 1.15 / 1.91x book. Rs 15.00 is 3.0x book, which would need a lasting ROE of about 38% at the base cost of equity.

models.name: Residual income
models.comment: Book value Rs 5.01 (September 2026). ROE moves from 22% (today's tariffs) to 9 / 16 / 22% within two years, as the tariff change comes within months, with 70% paid out, at a cost of equity of 15.7 / 14.2 / 12.7%. After that the excess return grows at 1.5 / 2 / 2.5%.

models.name: Dividends (two-stage)
models.comment: The 2026/27 dividend is Rs 0.40 / 0.60 / 0.75 (Rs 0.60 for 2025/26, none declared yet for 2026/27). It grows 0 / 1.5 / 2% for five years, then 1.5 / 2 / 2.5%, at a cost of equity of 15.7 / 14.2 / 12.7%; after year 5 the payout becomes 1 - growth / ROE. Cash after maintenance covered 2025/26's dividend 1.6 times.

modelsNote: Five methods, equal weight, all from scripts/valuation.py. Growth check: the plants support about 0% growth (capex outside the solar project was Rs 4mn in 2025/26 against Rs 128mn depreciation, and there are no capital commitments); the calculator's 109% reflects the one-off solar build, and the assumed 0 / 1.5 / 2% are within 2 points. NAV (Rs 5.01) is shown for reference only. The bear case is not a disaster case: if a contract were not renewed at all, that plant would earn nothing.

buyPlan.realism: Rs 4.87 needs a 68% fall. That is below every year-end price in the ten-year summary (lowest Rs 5.40 in March 2020) and far below the recent range (low Rs 11.60 in 2025/26, Rs 14.70 in July-September 2026), so the buy price is very unlikely to be reached unless the renewals go badly. A better trigger is the renewal announcement: if the tariff is at or near today's, fair value rises towards Rs 9-10.

higher: Kiriwaneliya and Denawaka renewed at or near today's Rs 25 a kWh (the bull case: about Rs 9.60 a share).
A new contract or tender win (battery storage, more solar) at a return clearly above 14%.
The CEB paying on time again, bringing the Rs 709mn of receivables back down.
A lower required return across the market (a falling bond yield).
lower: Renewal at Erathna's Rs 8.26 a kWh or lower, or a gap between expiry and renewal with no revenue.
Further solar curtailment by the grid operator, or a dry year for the hydro plants.
CEB arrears growing, turning profit into receivables rather than cash.
Borrowing for a new project at a low return, or cash paid out above what the plants earn.

notes.disclaimer: These are estimates from the annual report to March 2026 and the interim reports to June and September 2026. The renewal tariff for the two subsidiary plants is an assumption, not a disclosed figure. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.

fullText:
**Summary**

Vallibel Power Erathna PLC (VPEL.N0000) owns three mini-hydro plants (Erathna 9.9 MW; and, through its 87.2% subsidiary Country Energy, Denawaka 7.2 MW and Kiriwaneliya 4.65 MW) and a 10 MW solar farm at Dolahena, Matara, opened in September 2025. All the power goes to the state grid under standardised power purchase agreements (SPPAs). Vallibel Power Limited owns 40.08%.

It is a good business on the four tests: ROE 20-45%, net debt only Rs 0.32bn, no loss in ten years, and profit turns into cash. But at Rs 15.00 (last traded, 30 September 2026) the share is about 2.6 times my fair value of Rs 5.73. Buy price Rs 4.87 (fair value less 15%); strong buy Rs 4.29 (less 25%). Category: watch list (good business, price too high).

**The one thing that matters: two contracts expire within four months**

- Kiriwaneliya's 15-year SPPA ends in December 2026 and Denawaka's in February 2027. Together they earned Rs 921mn, 60% of 2025/26 revenue, on the avoided-cost tariff of about Rs 25 a kWh.
- Renewal is "subject to agreement" with the CEB, and management expects to renew "in line with prevailing regulatory provisions". No new tariff is disclosed, in the annual report or the September interim.
- The only evidence in the reports is the group's own Erathna plant, renewed in 2019 to 2039: it earns a plant-factor tariff of Rs 8.26 a kWh (Rs 353.5mn for 42.8 GWh).
- I value the first full year after renewal with the tariff at Erathna's level (bear, Rs 8.26), halfway (base, Rs 16.8) or unchanged (bull, Rs 25.4). EPS is then Rs 0.45 / 0.83 / 1.13, against a reported Rs 1.79 for the last twelve months.

**Latest results**

- Six months to September 2026: revenue Rs 1,107mn (+43%), owners' profit Rs 497mn (+17%), EPS Rs 0.66 (Rs 0.57). Solar brought Rs 231mn; hydro output was up at all three plants.
- September quarter: revenue Rs 571mn (+62%) but tax Rs 168mn (Rs 58mn), after the subsidiary paid the company a Rs 430mn net dividend; EPS Rs 0.30 (Rs 0.25).
- The CEB owed Rs 709mn at 30 September (Rs 214mn in March), Rs 140mn of it 60-180 days old; operating cash in the half was only Rs 84mn.
- 2025/26: revenue Rs 1,538mn (+12%), profit Rs 1,345mn (+21%) but profit before tax Rs 1,046mn (-32%). 2024/25 had Rs 479mn of CEB late-payment interest; 2025/26 had a Rs 421mn deferred tax credit from the solar plant's 100% capital allowance. Both flatter the trend.
- Solar farm: Rs 1,733mn, financed by Rs 1,296mn of Commercial Bank loans at 10.75-11.00% over seven years. Net debt Rs 0.32bn at September; NAV Rs 5.01.

**Valuation (Rs per share)**

| Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DCF of the plants + deferred tax and old-tariff months | 3.10 | 6.64 | 10.22 | 6.29 |
| P/E (first year after renewal) | 2.64 | 5.95 | 9.78 | 5.72 |
| Justified price to book | 2.65 | 5.75 | 9.58 | 5.59 |
| Residual income | 2.84 | 5.92 | 9.90 | 5.79 |
| Dividends (two-stage) | 2.61 | 5.42 | 8.72 | 5.24 |
| **Average** | **2.77** | **5.94** | **9.64** | **5.73** |

Weights 30 / 50 / 20. Cost of equity 15.7 / 14.2 / 12.7% (beta 0.58), WACC 15.6 / 14.1 / 12.7%.

**Key assumptions**

- Generation: Erathna 42 GWh, solar 20 GWh (18 in the bear case for grid curtailment), Denawaka and Kiriwaneliya 41 GWh (36 GWh, 2025/26's dry year, in the bear case).
- Solar tariff Rs 25.39 a kWh, fixed to 2045. Erathna Rs 8.26 to 2039.
- Cash costs about Rs 365mn a year, as in 2025/26 plus a full year of solar; depreciation Rs 167mn.
- Tax about 29%: 30% at the company, 15% plus 15% dividend withholding at the subsidiary. Minorities own 12.8% of the subsidiary.
- Growth 0 / 1.5 / 2% for five years, then 1.5 / 2 / 2.5%. The existing plants support about 0% growth (capex outside the solar project was Rs 4mn in 2025/26 against Rs 128mn depreciation; no capital commitments), so growth needs new projects, which the DCF charges at a 10 / 13 / 15% return on new capital.
- Long-run ROE 9 / 16 / 22%; dividend for 2026/27 Rs 0.40 / 0.60 / 0.75.
- Add-on: the Rs 171mn deferred tax asset (Rs 0.23 a share) and the few months left at the old tariff (Rs 0.08 / 0.04 / 0).

**What the price implies**

Rs 15.00 is 18 times base-case EPS after renewal and 13 times EPS even if today's tariff is kept. At a 14.2% cost of equity and 2% growth, no ROE justifies a P/E of 13 (the most is about 8). The market seems to expect renewal at today's tariff and a lower required return.

**Buy plan (500 shares)**

- 200 shares up to Rs 4.87, 150 up to Rs 4.60, 150 up to Rs 4.29: average about Rs 4.62, about Rs 2,310 in total (Rs 7,500 at today's price).
- Realism: Rs 4.87 needs a 68% fall, below every year-end price in the last ten years (lowest Rs 5.40 in March 2020). It is unlikely unless the renewals go badly. Watch the renewal announcement instead: at today's tariff, fair value is nearer Rs 9-10.

**What would change my view**

- Higher: renewal at or near Rs 25 a kWh; a battery-storage or new solar contract at a good return; the CEB paying on time.
- Lower: renewal at Erathna's Rs 8.26 or lower, or a gap with no revenue; more curtailment or a dry year; CEB arrears growing; a new project at a poor return.

**Management and plans**

The solar farm was built in the planned six months and is on track for more than Rs 500mn a year. Management plans to renew the two contracts, look at battery storage (it took part in a tender) and keep a "balanced" dividend. One of the two Joint CEOs resigned at the end of May 2026. Nothing has been said about the renewal terms.

**Shareholders**

Vallibel Power Limited 40.08% and Mr K.D.D. Perera 19.38% (printed K.A.D. Perera in March), unchanged. Public holding 40.52% with 8,863 holders (8,198 in March). Small buying by P.P. Subasinghe (+0.52mn) and Sampath Bank/Dr Dewolage (+0.45mn); DFCC Bank sold 0.62mn. SLIC's two holdings were renamed and total 38.0mn, as before.

**Uncertain or not found**

- The renewal tariff for Denawaka and Kiriwaneliya: not disclosed; the single biggest unknown.
- Share price: no CSE close in the site's price file for this share yet; Rs 15.00 is the last traded price the company reported for 30 September 2026.
- Beta: Damodaran's emerging-markets file couldn't be opened and no local 5-year betas were verified (provisional 0.58).
- The calculator's tax rate for 2025/26 is negative (one-off deferred tax credit), which slightly overstates the after-tax cost of debt.
